headline: Iran offers Hormuz reopening, Brent -7.3% Monday, 2s10s 20bp, Nasdaq record close
stance: Oil is trading the diplomacy now, not the blockade. Rates followed it lower; the front end did not move.

news.head: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within seven days
news.body: Offer reported Tuesday, conditional on the US lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. Sent through a mediator.

news.head: Treasury says Iranian airlines shut down from Wednesday
news.body: Bessent's warning landed Tuesday. Foreign airports, fuel suppliers and ticketing agents face secondary sanctions for serving them.

news.head: Trump held off Yemen strikes, open to an Iran meeting
news.body: Rejected Saudi calls to hit the Houthis. Said he would probably meet Pezeshkian at the UN assembly this week.

news.head: Saudi crude keeps moving through Hormuz
news.body: Exports ran 2.9 million barrels a day over six days, with the East-West pipeline still shut.

implications: Cheaper crude and a flatter curve arrived together Monday. The front end still prices the Fed, not the oil.
A reopened strait takes the risk premium out of corn, copper and crude, all pinned at three-year extremes.

watch.head: Philadelphia Fed services survey, 8:30
watch.body: The only US release today. Nothing in it for rates.

watch.head: Trump meets Gulf leaders, 2:45pm ET
watch.body: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman, in New York. Crude takes those headlines first.

watch.head: Trump addresses the UN General Assembly, Sep 23
watch.body: Iran's delegation is in New York through Sep 26. Any signal of a meeting moves oil before it moves rates.

watch.head: Job openings (JOLTS), September 29
watch.body: The next US release that can move rates. Headline risk fills the gap until then.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 2s10s flattened to 20bp Monday, the flattest since March 2025. The long end did the moving; the 2-year did not budge.
Overnight: 10-year 4.943%, 2-year 4.741%, 30-year 5.272% (~6am ET). Down about 2bp across the curve.
No FOMC until October 28. Iran headlines carry rates until then, not the US calendar.
sections.positioning: September 15 positioning: gold specs extended long, 95th percentile, seven weeks there. That is the position walking into de-escalation headlines.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Nasdaq-100 closed at a record Monday. Best session for it and for the S&P since August 4.
Breadth barely followed. 31.3% of S&P members sit above their 50-day, from 29.3% Friday.
Futures little changed overnight (~6am ET). No follow-through bid after the record close.
sections.positioning: Equity positioning sits mid-range on the September 15 report. No index extreme to lean against this week.

single_name.note: GameStop: two insider rules fired and it trades above its 200-day. 9.7 days to cover. On the list three sessions.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Bank reserves went back above $3tn on September 16, first time since July 22. The system is gaining cash into the quarter turn.
Fed balance sheet +2.1% year on year, from +0.8% in mid-June. Liquidity is not the constraint here.
IG spreads tightened 3bp last week. Credit never priced the Hormuz closure.

ideas.line: 5 open · 1 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
